newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids again mixed, LSFO still soft.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids again mixed, LSFO still soft.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices again were mixed again on Monday in thin trade, with sluggish utility demand still undermining the low sulphur market, while high sulphurs held steady or gained slightly, sources said.
"Unless we see crude dump again, we're not going to see much lower fuel numbers," said one cash trader, noting firm bunkers recently helped boosted high sulphur grades.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent again eased slightly to $15.00-$15.25 a barrel, with May one percent paper steady to modestly lower at $14.90-$15.10. June paper firmed about a quarter, with crude, to $15.25-$15.40, traders said.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour also was down slightly to $16.00-$16.25. New York Power Authority tendered for 100,000 barrels of high pour for April 17-25 delivery. Fixed price bids are due Tuesday at 1100 EDT.
NYH high sulphurs again gained ground, with three percent up slightly to the $14.25 area.
At the U.S. Gulf, three percent notionally held steady at $13.50, while one percent also was unchanged at $15.00-25.
Traders said a major was seeking bids for 35,OOO-50,000 barrels of prompt 2.8 percent (low vanadium, high gravity), but no deals were confirmed.

New York city gate gas prices were steady to up slightly Monday to about $2.40/mmBtu, or $15.12 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, also was modestly higher at about $2.00/mmBtu, or $12.60 a barrel.
